According to Chapter V (Applications), if a public officer or anyone sees a person attempting to cross a bridge ascertained to be unsafe and there is no time to warn him, they may seize him and turn him back. However, when there is not a certainty but only a danger of mischief, no one but the person himself can judge the sufficiency of the motive for incurring the risk, so he ought only to be warned—unless he is a child, or delirious, or in some state of excitement or absorption incompatible with the full use of the reflecting faculty.
